basis: Methionine synthase deficiency defines a metabolic disorder with megaloblastic anemia and neurodevelopmental impairment; hepatomegaly alone does not establish liver damage.
Malignant fibroblastic neoplasm arising in connective soft tissue; no additional organ involvement established across patients.
Primary movement disorder causing sustained dystonic contractions; muscle contractions alone do not establish primary muscle disease.
Defined ovarian metastasis lies outside the axes; the gastrointestinal or breast source is a separately diagnosed primary cancer.
Benign ovarian epithelial and stromal neoplasm; reproductive organs have no axis.
Hydrocephalus and skeletal abnormalities define the syndrome; aortic regurgitation is frequent (30-79%).
PRPF31-related retinal degeneration with night blindness and progressive visual loss; optic disc changes remain within the ocular axis.
Multiple desmoplastic trichoepitheliomas are cutaneous hair-follicle neoplasms.
Cloacal exstrophy affects bladder and hindgut; frontonasal skeletal malformation supplies the third axis. Definition and phenotype details are unavailable.
GNAT2-related retinal cone dysfunction causes achromatopsia and visual impairment.
IKZF1-related combined immunodeficiency with defining blood-cell depletion/pancytopenia; leukemia in 2/29 is a separate minority malignancy.
Malignancy of the epididymis, a reproductive organ without an axis; no consistent source organ is specified for metastatic cases.
Prenatal motor-neuron disease; contractures and clubfeet occur in 2/2, with muscle atrophy. Respiratory insufficiency reflects muscle weakness, not direct lung damage.
Immunodeficiency and learning/motor impairment define RIDDLE; pulmonary fibrosis is occasional (5-29%); recurrent respiratory infections are separate diseases.
Record mixes IRF8 deficiency and CAEBV; both support immune/blood-cell disease. Persistent liver dysfunction is described among the most common CAEBV features (>30%).
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; optic atrophy directly damages the visual system in 2/4 patients (50%).
Acute bronchiolar inflammation is usually a viral respiratory infection, commonly RSV.
Neoplasm of the maxillary sinus, included in the airway axis; lymphoma is only one subtype and does not define the umbrella.
Dermatitis, large-intestinal inflammation and synovial hyperplasia each occur in 1/1 assessed patients; frequency estimates are fragile. Recurrent infections are separate.
Cerebral arterial stenosis defines moyamoya; infarction or hemorrhagic brain injury occurs in roughly a third or more over the course. TIAs alone do not establish damage.
Specific phobia is a purely psychiatric condition; the neurological ancestor does not establish neurological organ damage.
Generic benign connective soft-tissue neoplasm; the definition does not specify cardiac or cutaneous origin.
Progressive neurodegeneration of language networks causes impaired word retrieval and repetition.
Lymphoid-cell malignancy involving the ureter; lymphoma supplies both blood-cell and immune mechanism axes.
Glycosylation-related myopathy; brain and eye damage characterize predominant muscle-eye-brain forms, supporting >30% across the group; mild limb-girdle forms may spare both.
